summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, recurrent cellulitis, PTSD, and depression was admitted with fever, myalgias, and diarrhea, followed by shortness of breath and left lower lobe pneumonia on chest X-ray. She was treated with ceftriaxone and azithromycin for bacterial pneumonia, while viral syndrome was considered the likely cause of her systemic symptoms. Stool studies were negative for C. diff, Salmonella, Shigella, and other pathogens, and blood cultures showed no growth. On hospital day 2, she developed transient volume overload with pleural effusions, likely due to IV fluids, which resolved after diuresis with Lasix. Her symptoms gradually improved, fever resolved, and she was discharged home on oral antibiotics with plans to complete a 7-day course. She remained on minocycline for stable leg cellulitis, continued her home medications, and was advised to follow up with her primary care and infectious disease providers.
